newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $66, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $66, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids were reported at mostly $65.00 per cwt, with a few at $66.00 but bids were passed by owners asking $67.00 to $68.00, feedlot sourrces said.
"We'ver got a few buyers out walking the yard taking inventory, but I don't think we'll see any trading today," a Texas Panhandle feedlot manager said.

Packers reportedly had adequate cattle to get through this week and were evaluating needs for next week, sources said. Part of the process included discovering how well beef moved out of retail meat cases over the holiday weekend. Early indications were inconclusive, cattle feeders and some wholesale meat sources said.
There was concern in the industry that cool, wet weather on Sunday and Monday in the U.S. Midwest and South put a damper on holiday cookouts and slowed beef consumption.
It could take several days to discover how well beef sold during the holiday weekend, market sources said.

"We hear stories that packers already are getting calls from retailers for replacement orders, but if that's true, the packer buyers we've seen this morning sure aren't acting like they need cattle," a Kansas feedyard manager said.
One source said that some packers had ample cattle bought for near-term needs.
Sources also noted that packers can start drawing on June contracted supplies after June 1.
"That could explain why he's (packers) not bidding too aggressively," the source said.
